logicalBugs.explanation: In Saleor, while creating a voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) restricted to eligible products, confirm an assignment of catalogue items such as a category, collection or product. The entire discount editor is replaced by an unexpected-error screen instead of retaining the selected items and allowing setup to continue. The trigger is confirming eligibility assignment on a new voucher, separately from applying filters inside an assignment dialog.

rootCause.explanation: VoucherCreatePage unconditionally maps the active catalogue tab through mapLocalVariantsToSavedVariants, whose mapper dereferences variant.product. Category and collection objects, and product objects themselves, are not variant-shaped; switching to these assigned-item tabs can therefore throw after assignment. This cause does not establish a crash for a correctly shaped variant or a filter submission.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Saleor, a failed voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) Save can still persist part of the edit: a new name or discount type can survive a rejected sales channel (a storefront/currency configuration) discount, and deleting an existing code can succeed while its duplicate replacement is rejected. Returning to the list and choosing Ignore changes does not undo those already committed edits.

rootCause.explanation: createUpdateHandler starts voucherUpdate, voucherChannelListingUpdate, code deletion and catalogue updates as independent promises and waits for Promise.all only after they have started. Errors are collected after independent commits, without a transaction, preflight barrier or compensation. The same orchestration produces metadata/channel partial writes and code replacement partial deletion; type changes can also race channel validation against the old discount type.

analysis.explanation: The detail save runs updateVoucher and updateChannels independently in Promise.all. The voucher type/name can commit while channel amount validation fails, and type changes do not revalidate existing channel values as one atomic mutation.

The detail update starts voucherUpdate and voucherCodesDelete independently in the requests array; deletion commits even if adding the replacement code fails. No transaction or compensation spans the calls.

rootCause.explanation: VoucherRequirements and VoucherLimits calculate invalid minimum quantity/usage-limit flags only for inline display. The shared createVoucherUpdateHandler gates submit using validateChannelListing and buildChannelListingLocalErrors, which contain neither of those non-channel checks. Consequently those displayed invalid fields reach the same submit path as valid data. This explains the missing submit gate for local quantity/limit errors. It does not prove why a server-rejected large quantity shows success: at the pinned revision VoucherDetails.handleSubmit collects mutation errors before notifying success, so that notification mechanism remains unresolved.

analysis.explanation: VoucherLimits derives hasInvalidUsageLimit for display only, while the save path submits hasUsageLimit/usageLimit without using that validation to stop the request; zero is then interpreted as an absent cap in display logic.

VoucherRequirements displays an error for a value below one but the submit handler does not stop on that UI-only condition; it forwards zero, which means no item requirement, and other independent successful updates can produce a success acknowledgement.

guidance.claimScope: Accept only the missing End Hour error indication when the combined end timestamp is invalid. The error wording and chronological validation are correct. This is distinct from stale errors after correction and post-success save-state bugs.

matchingScope.observableFailure: The report identifies missing invalid/error indication on End Hour, or misleading date-only highlighting, for the combined end-before-start timestamp conflict.

matchingScope.afterFix: When Start Date and End Date are the same and End Hour is earlier than Start Hour, Save highlights both End Date and End Hour as invalid. The same wording and chronological rejection remain valid.
matchingScope.wordingOnlyClaim: A complaint solely that the word date is wrong because calendar dates match does not establish this accepted failure.
matchingScope.mixedClaim: A report that establishes the missing End Hour error indication describes this accepted failure even if it also proposes clearer wording.

rootCause.explanation: The report establishes contradictory success and failed-save feedback for an invalid usage limit.
